learning: If the oval holds at 20/20 and the bends gain progress, finer sensing is useful and can be combined with a modest spread increase. If the oval drops or oscillation rises, return to 12 mm, since the baseline footprint is the stable choice.
notes: Complete package for the 8 mm footprint test. The geometry matches the Builder's proposal exactly, and the controller is the iteration-0 baseline unchanged.
rationale: The Builder's entity0 is a single-variable test against the iteration-0 baseline: the sensor footprint changes from 12 mm to 8 mm, and every other geometry value is unchanged. The baseline controller is kept exactly, so the footprint is the only variable. Iteration 0 is still the best design (356.6), with the oval at 20/20 in 1.65 s and oscillation 0.15. Its s-bend (0.17) and slalom (0.12) failures are at max_error of about 0.061 m, at the 0.06 m limit. Iterations 3 and 4 show the sensor row is very sensitive to lead: y=0.07 and y=0.03 both collapsed the oval to 0/20, so y=0.05 stays. Iterations 1 and 2 showed that the 0.5 kg mass and the wide array hurt the oval, so the drivetrain stays at 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track and 0.03 m radius. The 8 mm footprint leaves 4 mm gaps between sensors at 12 mm pitch. The 25 mm tape still covers at least one sensor at any offset, so the summed reading should not fall below 0.05 from gaps alone. Controller: kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction, unchanged. I expect the oval to stay near 20/20 at about 1.65 s, and the bends to improve only if finer edge resolution helps. Steering oscillation may rise with a more binary signal, and this is untested.
